items.q: A women's clothes store adds furniture for existing customers. According to Ansoff:
opts: Diversification
Market development
Market penetration
Product development
items.why: New product (furniture) sold to existing customers = Product Development. The product is new but the market/customers are the same. The key is: same customers (existing market) + new product category (furniture) = product development, not diversification (which would need new customers too).
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Which of the following is most likely to provide a business with a sustainable competitive advantage over a long period?
opts: A temporary price promotion that undercuts rivals
A patented production process that reduces unit costs significantly
Hiring staff away from a competitor for a short-term project
Matching a competitor's product features within six months of their launch
items.why: A patent provides legal protection, preventing rivals from copying the process, so the cost advantage can be maintained for the patent's duration. The other options are either easily replicated (matching features, hiring individuals) or deliberately short-term (price promotion), and therefore do not constitute sustained competitive advantage.
items.label: New question

items.q: Forward vertical integration would most address which of Porter's Five Forces?
opts: Buyer power
Entry threat
Rivalry
Substitute threat
items.why: Forward vertical integration means buying/merging with a business closer TO the customer (e.g. a manufacturer buying a retailer). This directly reduces buyer power because you now control the distribution/retail stage. Forward = towards the customer. If buyers have too much power, you buy them/their channel = reduce their leverage.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Statement 1: 'Lean production can improve cash flow by reducing levels of inventory.' Statement 2: 'Lean production can improve profitability by reducing waste.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Both true. Less inventory = less cash tied up in stock = better cash flow. Less waste = lower costs = higher profitability. These are two core benefits of lean production. Both are fundamental advantages of lean. Lower inventory improves cash flow; reduced waste improves profit margins.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Statement 1: 'Market penetration = existing product in new market.' Statement 2: 'Diversification = developing a new product OR entering a new market.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Both false. Statement 1: penetration = existing product in existing market (not new). Statement 2: diversification requires both a new product and a new market, not either/or. Diversification is the only Ansoff strategy requiring both new product and new market simultaneously. It's not an 'or' situation.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Statement 1: Horizontal integration can increase a firm's market share rapidly but may attract scrutiny from competition authorities.

Statement 2: Conglomerate integration reduces a firm's exposure to risk in any one market because its activities are spread across unrelated industries.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Both statements are true. Horizontal integration (buying a competitor) can quickly consolidate market share but may reduce competition, triggering a Competition and Markets Authority investigation. Conglomerate integration into unrelated sectors spreads risk so that poor performance in one industry does not devastate the whole business.
items.label: New question

items.q: A business gives a highly rewarded role to a trade union leader to overcome resistance. According to Kotter & Schlesinger:
opts: Education and communication
Explicit coercion
Facilitation and support
Manipulation and co-option
items.why: Giving a specific person a desirable role to win their cooperation = manipulation and co-option. Co-option specifically means giving a key resister a role in the change process. Co-option = giving someone a role to neutralise their resistance. It's a form of manipulation because the underlying concerns aren't addressed.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Each employee has a job with clear rules and procedures. This corresponds to which of Handy's cultures?
opts: Person culture
Power culture
Role culture
Task culture
items.why: Clear rules, procedures, and defined job descriptions = Role culture. This is the most bureaucratic and formal of Handy's cultures. Role culture = rules, procedures, hierarchy, formal job descriptions. Think: large government departments, traditional banks.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Halloran Retail plc has reported three consecutive years of falling profits. The board decides to close its ten least profitable stores, sell a non-core subsidiary and reduce its product range by 30%. This strategy is best described as:
opts: Diversification
Market development
Retrenchment
Forward vertical integration
items.why: Retrenchment involves a business cutting back its scale, scope or activities, typically to reduce costs and stabilise performance during a period of difficulty. Closing stores, divesting subsidiaries and narrowing the product range all fit this definition. The other options all involve expansion rather than contraction.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: A multinational corporation (MNC) is defined as a business that exports goods to more than one foreign country.
Statement 2: One reason host governments may welcome MNCs is that they can bring foreign direct investment and create local employment.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: An MNC is defined by having productive operations (not merely exports) in more than one country — Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 correctly identifies FDI and job creation as standard benefits that attract host governments to welcome MNCs. Students frequently confuse exporting with being a multinational.
items.label: New question

items.q: Strategy X: selling goods with positive YED. Strategy Y: reducing costs via economies of scope. Statement 1: 'X won't work if GDP declines.' Statement 2: 'Y only works with a wider product range.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Both true. Positive YED + falling GDP = falling demand, so Strategy X fails. Economies of scope require a wider product range (sharing resources across different products). Economies of scale = savings from volume. Economies of scope = savings from variety.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Nexo Energy, a UK firm, wants to enter the Brazilian market quickly but lacks local knowledge and wishes to limit its financial exposure. It agrees with a Brazilian company to share resources, risks and profits on a specific project. This arrangement is best described as:
opts: A hostile takeover
A franchise agreement
A joint venture
Backward vertical integration
items.why: A joint venture involves two or more businesses creating a separate arrangement to share resources, risks and returns on a defined project, which fits Nexo's situation exactly. A franchise involves licensing a brand/system to an operator; a takeover requires purchase of a controlling stake; backward integration means acquiring a supplier.
items.label: New question

items.q: Four products with different PED and YED (A: -1.5/-1, B: -1.5/+1, C: -0.5/-1, D: -0.5/+1). Price cut + income fall. Which has highest sales now?
opts: Product A
Product B
Product C
Product D
items.why: Product A: elastic PED (-1.5) means the price cut causes a large demand increase. Negative YED (-1) means falling incomes increase demand (inferior good). Both effects boost sales. You need both effects pushing sales UP. High PED magnitude = big boost from price cut.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: What are the features of a 'cash cow' in the Boston Matrix?
opts: High market share in a high-growth market
High market share in a low-growth market
Low market share in a high-growth market
Low market share in a low-growth market
items.why: Cash Cows: high market share + low-growth market. They generate steady, reliable profits with minimal investment needed. Cash Cows = reliable profit generators. High share + low growth = steady cash flow.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Which one of the following does not vary with output in the short-run?
opts: Total revenue
Total costs
Fixed costs
Variable costs
items.why: Fixed costs do not change with output in the short run - that is what makes them 'fixed'. Everything else varies with output.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Aldi pursues a strategy of offering a limited range of products at consistently low prices by keeping operating costs tightly controlled. According to Porter's generic strategies, which strategy is Aldi most likely following?
opts: Cost focus
Differentiation focus
Cost leadership
Differentiation
items.why: Cost leadership means achieving the lowest costs across a broad market so prices can be kept low or margins increased. Aldi targets a wide consumer market rather than a narrow segment, so the strategy is cost leadership rather than cost focus. Students sometimes choose cost focus because Aldi stocks fewer lines, but the breadth of its customer base is what determines it is a broad-scope strategy.
items.label: New question

items.q: Shareholders of Carrow Industries plc demand higher dividends, while the board wishes to retain profit to fund expansion. Which of the following best describes this situation?
opts: A conflict between short-term shareholder returns and long-term corporate growth objectives.
A conflict between the company's mission statement and its legal obligations under the Companies Act to act in the best interests of creditors rather than shareholders.
A principal–agent problem caused by a sole trader having unlimited liability, meaning personal assets are at risk whenever business debts remain unpaid.
A conflict between revenue maximisation and cost minimisation objectives, since cutting costs would reduce output and therefore lower the total sales revenue generated.
items.why: Shareholders seeking immediate dividends prioritise short-term returns, whereas retaining profit for investment reflects a long-term growth objective. This is a classic short- versus long-term objective conflict. The other options either misidentify the parties involved or describe entirely different concepts.
items.label: New question

items.q: Which of the following is most likely to cause diseconomies of scale as a manufacturing firm grows very large?
opts: The firm negotiates larger bulk-buying discounts from suppliers, reducing the average cost of raw materials as purchasing power increases with scale
Communication across departments becomes slower and more distorted
The firm spreads its fixed costs over a greater volume of output, lowering the fixed cost per unit and reducing overall average costs as production expands
Specialist machinery becomes economically viable to purchase, allowing the firm to automate production processes and improve efficiency at higher output levels
items.why: Diseconomies of scale occur when average costs rise as output increases, commonly because larger organisations suffer from coordination and communication problems. The other options all describe advantages of growth: bulk-buying discounts are purchasing economies, spreading fixed costs is a technical/financial benefit, and specialist machinery is a technical economy of scale.
items.label: New question

items.q: Which of the following statements best distinguishes kaizen from just-in-time as lean production techniques?
opts: Kaizen focuses on reducing stock-holding costs by systematically eliminating inventory waste, whereas just-in-time focuses on improving worker motivation through team-based problem-solving activities.
Kaizen is concerned with continuous incremental improvement in processes, whereas just-in-time is a stock management approach that aims to receive materials only as they are needed.
Kaizen eliminates all identifiable forms of waste across the entire value chain, whereas just-in-time is a narrower technique that targets only the specific waste arising from overproduction.
Just-in-time is primarily a people management technique that empowers workers to control production scheduling, whereas kaizen is used exclusively to manage and evaluate supplier relationships.
items.why: Kaizen and JIT are both lean tools but address different things: kaizen is an improvement philosophy involving all employees in making ongoing incremental changes, while JIT is specifically a stock and supply management system. Options A, C and D either reverse or misstate the purpose of one or both techniques.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: Organic growth is generally slower than external growth but allows a business to retain greater control over its culture and operations.

Statement 2: A takeover is always a form of organic growth because the acquiring business grows its own asset base.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is true: organic growth builds capacity from within, which is slower but preserves control over culture, quality and direction. Statement 2 is false: a takeover is external growth because it involves acquiring another separate business rather than developing the firm's own internal resources.
items.label: New question
